Hi Julien,

Following Hannah's note, some details on our controls and options that address Schrems II risks:

1) EU-only processing
- We offer Dedicated EU deployments: model inference, KV/prefix caches, and ephemeral working storage are provisioned in an EU region you select (e.g., eu-west-1, europe-west2). No inference requests are routed outside that region for dedicated tenants.

2) SCCs & contractual
- Redwood executes the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (controller-processor or processor-subprocessor as applicable). We also provide a Data Processing Addendum with residency and access commitments.

3) Encryption & key management
- Customer-managed keys (CMK) via customer KMS in the EU (support for major cloud KMS providers). Keys never leave the EU region; we support bringing-your-own-key so Redwood cannot decrypt without a key you control.

4) Technical safeguards
- Network isolation (VPC-only endpoints), private control plane option (Redwood Private) so metadata and orchestration can be kept inside your network.
- Role-based access controls (RBAC) and IAM scoping, with optional IP allowlists.
- Audit logs: detailed request/response telemetry, KV cache hits, admin actions. We can provide ISO/CSV extracts and Ship to your SIEM via secure syslog or S3 export.

5) Supplementary measures for transfers
- We provide contractual commitments, strong encryption in transit and at rest, and the option for additional encryption at the application layer (customer-side encryption).

6) Evidence package
- We can share: network topology diagram, summary SOC 2 report (redacted), PCA (processing commitments), and a sample SCCs annex for review. See attached: redwood-eu-data-protections.pdf

If helpful, we can prepare a short architecture diagram showing traffic flows and control boundaries for your legal team prior to contract review.

Cheers,

Marta / Julien —

Thanks — answering inline and proposing next steps below.

- Retention: default logs & telemetry retention is 90 days. We can support customer-configured retention windows (30/90/365) for inference metadata and logs as a Dedicated tenant option. For inference request/response retention used for quality monitoring, that is off by default; we only enable it with explicit customer opt-in in the contract.

- SCCs redline: we'll provide a sample redline of the processor-subprocessor addendum. Our legal is generally comfortable with standard SCCs + DPA; where customers request narrow changes we review on a case-by-case basis.

- Audit logs contents: exports include timestamps, request ids, model variant, token counts, latency, and error traces. Payloads (full inputs/responses) are not included in audit exports unless you enable retention for quality monitoring — in which case they are stored encrypted and subject to your retention settings.

- Schrems II mitigations: brief write-up attached (see redwood-eu-data-protections.pdf). Key points: CMK with EU KMS, private control plane option, contractual commitments, and ability to run a dedicated EU-only deployment.
